prompts: Create a NEW distinct Guangzong county town exterior for an ancient Three Kingdoms mobile exploration game. Use case historical-scene stylized game illustration. Portrait 1024x1536. Match the previously viewed Changshe reference's high-angle isometric miniature-like richly detailed warm sunlight, grey clay tiles, timber structures, earthen plaster, stone paths, lush green trees and natural materials. Do NOT copy Changshe composition or Xuzhou. Guangzong is a compact northern walled county town, distinct asymmetric branching street layout, sturdy grey stone and packed earth walls, civic compound upper LEFT, modest buildings not imperial palaces. No people, no written text, no labels, no UI. Seven readable individual entrances arranged with open space in front: county office walled modest compound upper left around x28 y24; post station with tethered horses lower right x78 y72; two-story inn upper right x75 y34; provisions shop awning sacks baskets center right x77 y51; blacksmith with anvil and spear racks middle left x24 y44; armor workshop displayed leather cuirass lower left x24 y62; records/roster office scrolls and wooden desk small building bottom left x25 y79. Broad clear central street and crossing plaza connects every door. Bottom center open gate and path exit at x50 y94. Upper right secondary gate at x80 y15 leads to distant small military tents beyond wall, for conditional campaign route. Keep all seven entrances individually legible, well separated and reachable. Building proportions and detailed handmade miniature rendering consistent with existing game, warm natural yellowgreen foliage, muted stone and grey roofs; no fantasy towers, no giant palace, no baked text plaques. Finish polished usable full-bleed scene illustration.

Edit this newly generated Guangzong game town to give it stronger local identity while preserving its excellent miniature isometric art style, warm daylight, portrait 1024x1536 dimensions and all seven buildings/doors at their current positions, clear road, gates, no text/no NPC. This is creative game art, not an archaeological reconstruction. Make it a NORTHERN AGRICULTURAL COUNTY TOWN near a campaign: outside top wall replace hills/rocks backdrop with flat wide yellow-green millet/wheat fields and low horizon landscape; less lush flowering garden greenery, more a few mature locust/elm-like shade trees and muted dusty green vegetation. Strengthen layered rammed-earth tan wall surfaces with grey stone foundation and patches of freshly repaired earth, restrained wear not ruins. Make the central plaza around the small tree into a compact EARTHEN GRAIN DRYING YARD on one side of the clear stone walkway: several woven reed mats with golden grain drying, winnowing baskets and a simple wooden grain cart beside provisioning shop, keep all access paths open. Add a small roadside straw-and-reed basket craft display near provisions shop, linen/hemp cloth hanging neatly by the inn side, clay storage jars and practical farming tools. Keep civic office recognizable upper left, inn upper right, forge middle left, armor shop lower left, records office bottom left, station with horses lower right. Distant small neutral military tents beyond top right secondary gate, modest stacked defensive timbers next to wall, hint of wartime readiness with calm civilian everyday life. Avoid southern water-town canals, ornate imperial palace, excessive bright flowers, modern objects, human figures, text and signs. Preserve strong readability of all seven doors and bottom exit. Polished coherent full scene, not object collage.

Edit this Guangzong county-town game scene. Keep portrait 1024x1536, same warm high-angle detailed miniature art, northern fields, rammed earth walls, all SEVEN existing service buildings, both gates, grain drying yard and readable road layout unchanged in purpose and recognizable location. Add THREE clearly separate modest RESIDENTIAL HOUSES, not more shops. Use small single-story plain timber/plaster houses with dark grey tiles and small fenced domestic yards, about half the mass of the inn. One house in the currently open rear strip immediately to the RIGHT of county-office compound and to the LEFT of the upper-right city gate, with domestic washing line. Second house behind/adjacent left edge of the armor workshop, offset back with a kitchen chimney and stacked firewood, keep armor workshop entrance clear. Third small residence along the right inside wall near the lower-right horse station, behind the station or tucked into bottom-right corner, with tiny vegetable patch and clay water jars. May subtly widen/deepen side neighborhoods to fit homes naturally while retaining full clear central walking route and no house blocking gate or shop. Domestic houses must be visibly identifiable as three distinct buildings with doors, small windows and modest private yards, not decorative roof fragments or goods stalls. Keep no people/no text/no UI. Avoid crowding; this is a functioning civilian county town with seven facilities plus a few ordinary homes. Do not remove or convert records office, armor shop, forge, inn, county office, post station or provision shop. Preserve artwork quality, consistent scales and lighting.
